newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up on spinners' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up on spinners' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Wednesday on renewed demand by spinners amid fears of short supplies of quality stock, dealers said.
"Fresh buying by spinners on the first day of the year pushed prices up," dealer Mustafa Hussain said. The rates might continue to rise amid widespread fear that quality stock would soon be out.
In the kerb market, the MNH-93 variety was traded at 2,400 rupees ($59.67) per maund (37.32 kg) and the K-68 at 2,375 rupees per maund, the dealer said.
